name: en_chinmaya_day09
transcript: Sahana bhavatu, sahano bhunaktu, sahaviryam karavavahai te Om Shanti. Shanti Shanti Om Yam Brahma Varunendra Rudra Marutah Tunvanti Divyai Stavaih Vedai Sangapadakramopanishadaih Gayanti Yam Samagaha Dhyanavasthita tadgatena manasa pashyanti yam yoginah yasyantam na vidussurasuraganah Devaya tasmai namah. Devaya tasmai namah. After having given the knowledge of the self, and also after having given the technique to prepare the mind to receive the self knowledge. So after having given in in gist, Gnana Yoga and Karma Yoga, then Bhagwan gives what are the signs of progress in spirituality. So as a person progresses in spirituality, he becomes more and more dispassionate. There is more and more clarity with regard to thinking. There is freedom from all kinds of delusion. And also there is abidance in the self. So then when Arjuna listens to this, discourse by Bhagwan. He develops an interest to know the man of realization. So Arjuna asks Bhagwan, Please describe a man of realization. What are his characteristics? How does he respond to the world? In what way he's different from us? In what way he carries himself in this world, meeting the day-to-day problems. So answering this question, Bhagwan says, Arjuna, the central What you call characteristics of a Mahatma is Atmanyevatmana Tushtaha. He's totally contented in the self. This contentment, this peace, this joy which he experiences in his own self. It expresses in various ways. How does it express? It expresses as no more desires in the outer world. He's able to give up all worldly desires. And moreover, he remains unaffected by the ups and downs of life. Life keeps on giving him dukha and sukha just like any other person in life in this world. But what is his attitude? Dukheshu anudigna manaha. The mind is not disturbed in dukha and moreover the mind doesn't crave for sukha. What is the state of mind? Vita raga bhaya krodhaha. A mind which is free from all negativities like attachment, like fear, anger. etcetera. And how does he carry himself in this world? Sarvatra anabhisneha, free from any kind of attachment to anything or anyone. Freedom from attachment. And therefore, he's able to withdraw his senses at will from the world just like a tortoise. He's able to withdraw his mind and the senses at will. will. So this is the way in which he carries himself in the world, remaining unattached everywhere. Now Bhagwan takes a slight digression from the topic. Now some of the verses are meant for the Sadhakas. How to gain this mastery over the senses and why the mastery over the senses is absolutely essential for a seeker of knowledge. This is the topic for almost the next 10 verses. So first, let us see the next three verses. Vishayavinivartante niraharasya dehinah rasavarjam rasopyasya param drushtva nivartate yatatohyapi kaunteya Purushasya vipashchitah indriyani pramathini haranti prasabham manah tani sarvani sanyamya yukta asit matparah Vashhehi yasyendriyani tasya prajna pratishthita. Yes. So here, Bhagwan gives the importance of controlling the sense organs. Arjuna, there is no choice. So instead of taking 59th verse first, we will take 60. We'll take 60 and then we'll go back to 59. So what does verse number 60 says? Yatato hyapi kaunteya purushasya vipashchitah. So a seeker who is Vipasshitaha, Vipasshitaha means wise, knowledgeable, he has studied all the scriptures, he has understood the logic, he is thoroughly convinced. So he is a knowledgeable person. He has attended satsang. He has understood the message of the scriptures. And therefore he is a knowledgeable person and yatataha api he is striving also. It's not that he is not striving, he is not a lazy person. and he's striving in the right direction. But Arjuna, indriyani pramadhini, all these indriyas or pramadhini is very, very turbulent. So therefore, there is absolute necessity to discipline them. If you don't discipline them, haranti prasabham manaha. It just forcefully loots away the mind. It disturbs the mind. Whatever little peace you have got through your Sadhana, everything will go away if you don't discipline your sense organs. So Bhagwan is very very insistent upon this. Disciplining the sense organ means practicing Dhamma. Now what is practicing Dhamma? As a spiritual seeker, it is our Prime duty and responsibility to see that the mind is always peaceful and quiet, because only when the mind is peaceful and quiet, higher contemplation is possible. So in order to keep this mind fit for doing Sadhana, what has to be done? You have to be very careful with regard to what kind of world you are exposing your senses to. In this world, there are good things, there are bad things. In this world, there are spiritually uplifting things. There are spiritually destructive things. Everything is available in this world in the form of Television in the form of internet, in the form of books, in the form of various kinds of company, people, you are constantly exposing yourself to the world. Bhagwan is telling, beware, be choosy. There are things which can pollute the mind, there are things which can elevate the mind. You have to be very, very, very choosy when it comes to exposing yourself to the world. Everything is there in the world, every type of people are in the world. Indriyani pramadini, if you indiscriminately expose yourself to the world, chances are that whatever little progress you have made, you will lose everything. Indriyani pramathini, they are very turbulent, they are capable of destroying your peace completely. So therefore, beware. Now this, we can in our own life we can see. You watch some third rate movie and then just sit for 10 minutes in meditation, just see your state of mind. You involve in some gossip, come back, sit for some time with yourself with closed eyes. You will see how much the mind has been polluted. Read some third rate novel, sit for some time in meditation. You will see how much the mind has been disturbed. It is something which we can in our own life, in our own experience we can find. It is not something very new to us. Bhagwan is saying, pay very much attention to this. As a seeker, you can't just go and mingle with everything and everyone. You have to be extremely careful. Just like a small sapling has to be protected with the fence. In the same way, in the beginning of Sadhana, we have to protect our mind by disciplining our senses. Because all the negativities they enter through the sense organs, especially the eyes and the ears. So we have to be extremely careful, only the filtered things should get in. That's why in Upanishad that Shanti mantra itself says, Bhadram Karnebi Shrunayama, Bhadram Pashyema Akshabiryajatraha. Oh Lord, may we hear only the auspicious things, may we see only auspicious things. This is the prayer because all the negativities are whether good or bad. They enter mainly through the eyes and the ears. So we have to be extremely careful. Then Bhagwan gives one more. Very useful tip for the Sadhaka. Verse number 59 you come now. Vishaya vinivartante niraharasya dehinaha. So such a seeker who is very careful with the kind of world he is exposing to. A serious spiritual seeker, such a spiritual seeker is called here as Niraharah. Niraharah means what? The one who doesn't take Ahara. Literally, Ahara means food. So here, a spiritual seeker who is not polluting his mind through his senses, such a person is called a Nirahara. Meaning, he doesn't give Ahara to the sense organs. Each and every sense organ demands certain ahara, food. What is the food which the eyes demand? Color and form. What is the food which the ears demand? sound, isn't it? So actually we are feeding our sense organs when we are exposing ourselves to the world. So here the seeker is called a Nirahara, meaning he doesn't feed junk into his sense organs. He's very careful with regard to the food he eats. It is not just that what you call mouth food which you are talking of. We are talking of the food with respect to each and every sense organ. So such a person who is very careful with what he is feeding his sense organ, such a diligent seeker is called here as Nirahara. So what happens when when you become nirahara? When you control your senses, vishaya vinivartante, automatically since you are not showing interest in the sensuous worldly things. Automatically they will recede. Either they will recede or you will recede. In short, what will happen? The sense objects will not come in contact with your senses. You are protected. But Arjuna, Even though you are protected from the external influence, external polluting influence, you are protected, no doubt, but still rasavarjam. Rasavarjya means there are so many negative asanas already there. Now they will start troubling you. External world will no more trouble you because you are cut off from it. Now who will trouble you? The rasa. which is already there in the mind. The vasanas, the negative vasanas, that will gargle up. Because of so many years, so many births you have exposed those senses to those negativities. So all those negativities are there in the mind in the form of various kinds of vasanas. Kama, krodha, lobha, moha, madamassery, everything is there, they will start gargling up and you will have a natural inclination and taste for it. Because it has become your habit. Those negativities because it has become your habit, it will be expressed now and then. That rasa, that taste for it will be there. The taste for the sensual indulgences will be there. It won't go away. But then Arjuna, don't worry. Why? Asya rasahaapi param drushtva nivartate. Even though these negativities are there, but as you keep doing your Sadhana, as the mind starts experiencing the higher joys of meditation, of devotion, etcetera, slowly that mind which is, which has, which is tasting the higher will start leaving the lower. Param drishtva, having seen the highest, nivartate. That rasam also will go away. Don't worry. So what is the first step? Cut off from the negative influences of the world. How do you cut off? by not exposing your sense organs. This is the first step to be done by any beginner in spirituality. If you know that certain place will pollute your mind, don't go there. If you know that certain books, certain TV programs or website of the what you call internet will pollute your mind, don't go. Now this is called Dhamma. This is the first step to be done. Then after that, deal with the negativities of the mind. How? by meditating upon the higher. Whatever negativity is already there, it will go. As the mind starts tasting the higher, all the negativities of the mind will automatically go. You need not worry. Therefore, verse number 61. Tani sarvani sanyamya yukta asita matparaha. May that seeker, tani tani indriyani sarvani sanyamya having controlled, having disciplined all the senses, sanyamya having disciplined them, may such a person. Yukta asita mat paraha, may he consider me as the highest and may he be seated. So after having disciplined the senses, what you should do? Now the mind has nothing to do because the mind is no more indulging in the world, mind is free, what you should do with the mind? Don't keep it idle. What has to be done? Let the mind contemplate upon me. Let it meditate upon me. Don't keep it idle. Arjuna, vashye yasyendriyani tasya prajna pratishthita. Such a person who has his indriyas under his control, the mind under his control, such a person will have a Clear intellect, what you call, he is called a sthita prajna. A person who has total mastery over his mind and the senses. Now Bhagwan, tell me one thing. What happens to the person who doesn't pay attention to any of these instructions? He totally indulges in everything of the world, what happens to him? So the next verses talk about the ladder of fall. How we fall in our life when we are indiscriminate with respect to our sensuous indulgences. Next verses, very famous verses. Let us chant. Dhyayato vishayan pumsah sangas teshu pajayate. Sangat sanjayate kamah. Kamaat krodhobhijayate krodhaat bhavati sammohah sammohat smritivibhramah Smriti bhramshat buddhi nashah, buddhi nashat pranashyati. Yes. So here is a ladder of fall of all those people who live. a licentious life. So what is the first thing? Dhyayato vishayan pumsaha. So here is a person who is intelligent, who is sensuous, so naturally what kind of thoughts will arise in his mind? Whatever way you have trained your mind, that way it will behave. Bas. What will be the nature of your mind? The nature of your mind will depend upon In what direction you have trained the mind. What all kinds of thoughts you have entertained in the mind. That will become the swabhava of the mind. So a saintly person will have only divine thoughts, mainly divine thoughts. A criminal person will have only criminal thoughts. There is such a big difference between the quality of a mind of a good person and a bad person. Who has decided this quality? We ourselves. So as far as a sensuous person is concerned, what kind of thoughts he will have most of the time? It will be the thoughts related to the vishayas. So therefore, dhyayato vishayan pumsa means the person meditates upon vishaya, some sense pleasure, some sensuous object. So here meditation means thinking. All the time a sensuous person will be meditating upon having the thoughts upon some sensuous object. So now the first step is vishaya dhyanam which is natural for a licentious man. Then what happens? With that vishaya dhyanam, next one. Sangaha tesho upajayate. From that comes Sangha. Sangha means desire. In this context, Sangha means desire. So when you think of a sense object, When you think of it, you come to know, oh, this sense object has the ability to give me happiness. So since this object has the ability to give me happiness, automatically what comes, you tend to desire for that object. Desire comes. You imagine about that sense object and you remember all those past experiences. In the past, this sense object has given me happiness. So let me gain that happiness again by indulging in it. This desire to indulge in that object is called Sangha. Then what happens? Slowly, slowly again and again you are thinking of that object. Slowly, slowly the momentum, the flux, the intensity of the thought becomes more and more. Then sangat sanjayate kamaha, third step. The very same Sangha takes the form of Kama. Here, Kama means intense craving. Intense craving, that mild desire becomes intense craving. Now what do you mean craving? Craving is that state where you feel without this I just can't live. It is a state of helplessness. Earlier the desire was only in the mind, now the desire has become so strong that it starts taking expression through the body. Meaning, now the person has no control over himself, the physical body literally goes to indulge in that object. This kama forces the person towards that object to indulge in it. So, kama means extremely forceful desire which a person cannot control. Now, after kama what should come? There are two possibilities. Either you will get the object or you will not get the object. These are the two possibilities. He's literally trying everything to get that object. Now if you get that object, what will happen? You will indulge in it and whatever addiction is there, that addiction will become a little more. After every indulgence, addiction is a little more. There the matter ends. For some time, he is relieved after indulgence. Now that branch is not taken up by Bhagwan. What is the other option? Sensuous object is there, somebody is preventing me from indulging in it. Because most of the time, 99% of the time it is something immoral, something adharmic, something unrighteous. You are creating trouble for others in the process because the kama has no eyes. Then what happens? Somebody comes, prevents you from indulgence. What happens to this kama? The very same intense attachment takes the form of krodha. Kamat krodhah abhijayate, it becomes intense anger. Greater the intensity of kama, greater will be the intensity of krodha also. And what happens when krodha comes? Krodhat bhavati sammohaha. Not just moha, sammoha. Total delusion. Meaning what? In that moment of anger, what is right, you see as absolutely wrong. What is wrong, you see as absolutely right. This is called Moha. Delusion is always atasmin tadbuddhihi. What is there you don't see, what is not there you see it. Sammohat smriti vibhramaha. Smriti vibhrama means loss of memory. All those things which you know. It is no more of any use. You might have studied scriptures, that knowledge is of no use. Whatever knowledge you have, which would have guided you rightly, that knowledge is no more available for you. Smriti bhramshat buddhi nashah. Now the Buddhi also gone. Buddhi takes decision what is right, what is wrong, etcetera based on the past experience, based on knowledge, since knowledge is no more available. Buddhi is also not able to take right decision. In fact, it takes wrong decision. Buddhi nashat pranashyati. With the destruction of intellect that person pranashyati means he perishes. The whole thing to understand, let us take a simple example. Examples can be multiplied. Plenty are available in this world. Let us take a very simple example. So there is this child. He's studying in some standard, maybe eighth standard, ninth standard, whatever. Tomorrow is the exam day. So what is he supposed to do? He's supposed to study. And he's studying also. But then, He's addicted to one thing, and that is playing video games etcetera in the mobile phone. Everyday he has been doing it. And as he was studying, suddenly, "Dhyayato vishayan pumsah". This thought came, let me play for some time. Exam is tomorrow. Let me play for some time. First, it was only a desire. Why not play for some time? It will be refreshing for me. I'm already tired studying this that, whatever. One desire, that is called as Sangha. Now again and again you are constantly thinking about it that Sangha becomes Kama. So he was in his room, there the mobile is not there. To get the mobile he has to go to his father's room. Father's mobile he used to play. So what happens? That Kama forces him to leave his room and go to his father's room. He goes there, mobile is there on the table, he takes it and starts playing. As he starts playing his mother comes. What are you doing? Tomorrow is the exam and you are in this. Mother started shouting. Like any other mother. Now what happens? As he was listening to the shouting, this irritated mother is shouting loudly. This irritation naturally passes on to him also. He was also irritated, he became so angry. Now what happens when anger comes? See all this. Sammohaha. Means what? What mother is telling is right actually. He is supposed to study for the exam. He should know that what he's doing is wrong. Sammoha means a feeling that what I'm telling, what I'm doing is right, she is wrong. Actually, it is the reverse. She is right and he is wrong. But when that sammoha comes, you feel you are right and she is wrong. Meaning, the very same person who is your own mother, who is your well-wisher, becomes the greatest enemy. Now see this is sammoha. What is there is your well-wisher and what are you seeing? Your greatest enemy. Sammoha Smriti Vibhramaha Sammoha Smriti Vibhrama Smriti gone. What is Smriti? This mother has taken care of me so much. Whatever I am today it is because of her sacrifice. So much she has done for me, I should be grateful to her. Everything gone, smriti vibhrama, loss of memory. I forget everything what she has done to me. Then, smriti bhramshat buddhi nashah. What does the buddhi normally say? I must respect my mother, I must love my mother, I must obey my mother. This is what the buddhi say. Now the buddhi is no more there. Buddhi nashat pranashyati. Now because of that irritation, now this is a real incident. He takes that mobile and bangs it on her head. Out of that irritation, out of that anger, because this mother is shouting. She takes that mobile and what you call with great force she banged it on her head. It struck on her head. She fell down unconscious. Blood was flowing. Immediately she was admitted to the hospital. After that this boy realized what a big mistake I have done, but it was too late. Now this is called Pranashyati. Now see, everything gone, mobile gone. Mother in the hospital. Now with this state of mind can he study? Study gone. This is called Pranashyati. Now see that ladder of fall. If he had in the beginning itself while studying when that thought came, let me play. If only he could have corrected there, This danger could have been stopped. Why he could not correct there? He could not correct there because this playing had become an addiction. Why it has become an addiction? Indiscriminate use of that mobile phone. Indriyani pramadhini. That was the reason. So see the ladder of fault. So that's why Bhagwan says be very careful with respect to using this sense organs. It can become your greatest enemy, it can totally destroy you. But suppose you have total mastery of your mind and the senses, then what will happen? The ladder of rise is presented next. Let us chant the next two verses. Ragadweshaviyuktaisthu vishayanindriyaischaran aatmavashyervidheyatma prasadamadhigacchati prasade sarvadukhanam Hanirasyo pajayate prasanna chetasohyaso buddheh paryavatishthate. Yes. On the other hand. Raga dwesha vyaktaihi tu. Tu means on the other hand. On the other hand. Now we are going to discuss about the ladder of rice. So what is that first term? Vidheyatma. He has kept his mind and the senses fully under control. A perfect Sadhaka. So whenever the mind has a desire, immediately because he is a regular meditator, regularly he does his Sadhana. Morning and evening he has time for it. He does his prayer, he does his meditation, etcetera, etcetera, and therefore one part of the mind is always looking within. When you regularly do your Sadhana, you develop the ability to look within. So what happens when you develop this ability to look within, whatever happens inside, very early stage you come to know. It is not in that in a Sadhaka, Kama, Krodha, etcetera, it doesn't come, it comes. But the beauty is even when it raises its hood, A Sadhaka is aware of it at a very early stage. One thought, two thought, four thought, eight thought, 16, 32, 64. As it becomes two, four, etcetera, he knows it. Because one part of his mind is paying attention within. So whatever is happening in the mind, he knows. As it builds up, immediately he comes to know, immediately he diffuses the danger. Negative thought is rising, immediately he replaces the negative with positive. In him that alarm bell rings at a very early stage. The red signal comes, and since he's aware at a very early stage, he is able to correct it at a very early stage. Correction at the early stage is very easy. Detection at the very early stage is very difficult. If you are able to detect at a very early stage, you can very easily correct it at that early stage. And this early detection is possible only if you do your Sadhana regularly because it is an ability, it is a Samarthya, it's a capacity to look within. It is something which can be developed over a period of time. Regular meditation will give you this ability to look deep within what is happening in your subconscious mind. And when you are able to see what is happening in your subconscious mind, you are able to correct it easily. And once correction is made there, you are safe. Because everything comes from thoughts, from the subconscious mind, the thoughts come into conscious mind, and from the conscious mind the thoughts take the form of words, thoughts take the form of actions. This is how it. You know, gains momentum. The subtle becomes gross. This is how it comes out. So as far as a Sadhaka is concerned, he is a Vidheyatma. Vidheyatma means what? Mind and the senses totally under control, disciplined. So he knows what is he doing. He's very much aware of what kind of thoughts are passing through the mind. He's a master of himself. Such a person, Bhagwan says, even when vishayan charan. Indriyaihi vishayan charan even when he is roaming around in the field of sense objects with his indriyas with his sense organs. Even when he's amidst sense objects, but what kind of sense organs he has? Atmavachyaihi, fully under his control. Raga dwesha vyuktaihi, those senses which are free from likes and dislikes. This is the kind of senses, sense organs he has. Those sense organs which are free from raga and dwesha, likes and dislikes, those sense organs which are totally under his control, with such a disciplined indriyas even when he is amidst sense objects. What is the state of mind? Prasadam adhigacchate. His experience is prasadam. Prasadam means cheerful mind, a peaceful mind. See that? Even when he's amidst sense objects, he's undisturbed. What about the other person? He's not amidst sense object, just one thought of sense object, he's destroyed, pranashyati. Here, even when he's amidst sense objects, nothing can touch him. It is like wearing the raincoat and going in the rain. The rain is not able to touch you. Or it's like applying oil and cutting jackfruit. That sticky thing doesn't touch you, isn't it? In the same way, when you move around in the world, It may be potentially polluting atmosphere also, but this person comes out unpolluted because the senses are so disciplined. Such a person prasadam adhigacchati. Why this prasadam, this peaceful mind, this cheerful mind, why is it important? Prasade sarva dukhanam hanirasyopajayate. What is the definition of a peaceful mind? A mind where there is sarva dukhanam haani. Absence of all sorrows. Absence of all negativities. Such a mind is called a cheerful mind, a peaceful mind. So every moment this person is enjoying such a healthy, peaceful, cheerful mind. What is it that you moment to moment enjoy? What is that which you enjoy every moment? Your cheerful, peaceful mind is the one thing you enjoy, isn't it? A person may be there in the seven-star hotel, but if the mind is not in good condition, his condition is miserable. Who cares? Where you stay, you may be in a hut, but if the mind is cheerful and peaceful, you are the happiest man, you are the richest man. Prasade sarva dukhanam hanirasya upajayate. What is the benefit of this cheerful and peaceful mind? Prasanna chetasaha hyaasu buddhi paryavatishthate. The greatest benefit of a peaceful, cheerful mind is with that mind you can Attempt for the highest. Contemplation becomes very easy for you because the mind is obedient. Mind listens to your instruction. Mind is available for higher contemplation, higher meditation, and with higher meditation, you gain the right knowledge. With right knowledge, your intellect becomes firm. You become a sthita prajna. To become a sthita prajna, what is absolutely essential is a peaceful mind. In fact, the peace and knowledge, they are connected. If you have a peaceful mind, you gain greater clarity with regard to knowledge. With greater clarity, greater the peace. With greater the peace, greater the clarity. Isn't it? Ultimately what happens, you experience infinite peace and firm abidence. This is where it leads you to. Only with a cheerful, peaceful mind, any sadhana is possible. And to have that peaceful mind, your senses must be disciplined. So this is that ladder of rice. The one who disciplines his senses, he will have a cheerful mind, and because he has a cheerful mind, he is able to do all the Sadhana, and because he is able to do the Sadhana, Shravana Mani Dhyasana is possible only when your mind cooperates with you. That's only possible when the mind is peaceful, and the mind is peaceful only when your senses are disciplined. So finally through Shravanam and Vidhyasana, you attain the highest ladder of rise. You become a Jivan Mukta, you become a Videha Mukta. So what has to be done? First aid has to be given in the beginning. What is the first aid? Control your senses. Again Bhagwan says, if the person doesn't control his senses, he had it next to us. Nasti buddhirayuktasya nachayuktasya bhavana nacha bhavayatasshantihi ashantasya kutassukham. Let us see this first. Nasti buddhihi ayuktasya. Ayuktasya buddhihi nasti. Ayuktaha means unintegrated one. What do you mean unintegrated one? Unintegrated one means the one who lives a loose life. No discipline with regard to any of his sense organs. A person who lives an indisciplined, immoral, sensuous life, such a person is called Ayuktaha. There is no integration. Integration means what? There is no oneness, oneness between his mind and the intellect. Intellect says something is right, but the mind is liking something else and he listens to his mind. They are not one. Very many times I like something but it is wrong. I dislike something but it is right. So what I should do? Should I listen to mind or intellect? Intellect says what is right and what is wrong. Mind says what I like and what I don't like. Whom should I listen? I should listen to the intellect, but this fellow listen to his mind. Whatever I like, I will do. According to him, that is freedom. Doing what you like is freedom, according to him. Pujya Gurudev says, not doing what you feel like doing is freedom. What is true freedom? Not doing what you feel like doing is freedom. Doing what you like, it is addiction. It is not freedom, it is slavery. So Ayuktaha, Ayuktaha means totally disintegrated one. He values something, but he has no courage to live up to it. An immoral, sensuous person. What happens to him? Ayuktasya buddhi hi nasti. For him, there is no buddhi. Why he has no buddhi? He has never used buddhi, that's all. What you constantly use, you will have it. What you don't use, you will lose it. Bhagwan also thinks, poor fellow, he's not using his buddhi, why unnecessarily give him? Let him, let me take it back. No buddhi means no knowledge. Buddhi develops only when you constantly use it and live according to its dictates. Everyone has got the buddhi. Intellect is there in every one of us. It is constantly guiding us also. But the question is, are you listening to it? If you don't listen, slowly, slowly, that buddhi becomes blunt. It becomes dim. The sensuous vasanas make it dim, like the torch, you know, when that battery is dying, what happens to that light? Battery dies down, that light also becomes dim. In the same way, the Buddhi also becomes dim. So Bhagwan says, Ayuktasya Buddhi hi nasti. And without this Buddhi, Nacha Ayuktasya Bhavana. Higher contemplation and meditation is called here as Bhavana. Because there is no Buddhi, how is it possible for him to do higher meditation? For doing higher meditation, you must have first done Shravana, listening to the knowledge of the scriptures. Only through Shravana, knowledge will come, but he has no Buddhi, no knowledge is there, then what will he meditate upon then? Meditation is impossible, contemplation is impossible, his mind is always rooted in everything lower. His baser passions are active in his mind. Lower passions are active.
